title: Domain of a Rational Function Containing a Radical in the Denominator
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain of the function defined by y = (x + 3) / (4 - sqrt(x^2 - 9)).

steps.title: Enforce Non-Negativity of the Radicand
steps.explanation: For the square root sqrt(x^2 - 9) to be real, we require x^2 - 9 >= 0, which holds when |x| >= 3, i.e., x <= -3 or x >= 3.
steps.why: Even-indexed radicals are defined in the real numbers only where their radicands are non-negative.

steps.title: Exclude Zeros of the Denominator
steps.explanation: Set the denominator not equal to zero: sqrt(x^2 - 9) != 4. Squaring both sides gives x^2 - 9 != 16, or x^2 != 25, which excludes x = -5 and x = 5.
steps.why: Division by zero is undefined, so any input that makes the denominator equal zero must be removed from the domain.

steps.title: Intersect Both Conditions
steps.explanation: Removing the points x = -5 and x = 5 from (-inf, -3] U [3, inf) splits each half-line into two intervals, yielding the union of four intervals.
steps.why: The natural domain of a compound expression is the intersection of the domains of all its constituent operations.
